Duncan Robinson was born on April 22, 1994.
Duncan Robinson is from York, Maine.
Duncan Robinson's parents are Elisabeth and Jeffrey Robinson.
Duncan Robinson has two siblings: Marta and Eli.
Duncan Robinson is part Hawaiian on his mother's side.
Duncan Robinson attended Rye Junior High School.
Duncan Robinson elected to attend The Governor's Academy in Massachusetts instead of Portsmouth High School.
Duncan Robinson began his freshman season as a 5-foot-7-inch (1.70 m) point guard for The Governor's Academy in 2008.
Duncan Robinson did not play much until he became "serviceable" as a junior at The Governor's Academy.
Duncan Robinson practiced shooting for hours, attempting to make 1,600 shots per week during his early years.
Duncan Robinson started working with trainer Noah LaRoche during his junior season.
Duncan Robinson averaged 18.5 points as a senior at The Governor's Academy.
Duncan Robinson was selected to the 2012 All-NEPSAC Class B first team and the 2012 All-Independent School League (ISL) team as a senior at The Governor's Academy.
Duncan Robinson graduated with a 3.55 GPA from The Governor's Academy.
Duncan Robinson played on the spring and summer Amateur Athletic Union (AAU) circuit after his senior season.
Duncan Robinson did a postgraduate year at Phillips Exeter Academy to increase his college prospects.
Duncan Robinson led Phillips Exeter Academy to a 28–1 record, ending on an 18-game win streak that included the NEPSAC Class A title.
Duncan Robinson posted 24 points and 10 rebounds in the championship game of Phillips Exeter Academy.
Duncan Robinson earned the Tournament MVP award at Phillips Exeter Academy.
Duncan Robinson was selected to the 2013 New England Preparatory School Athletic Council (NEPSAC) Class A All-League first team.
Duncan Robinson measured 6 feet 6 inches (1.98 m) and 175 pounds (79.4 kg) before his senior season at Phillips Exeter Academy.
Duncan Robinson grew to 6 feet 8 inches (2.03 m) and 195 pounds (88.5 kg) by the end of the summer after his senior season.
Division III Williams made Duncan Robinson an offer that he accepted immediately during a campus visit in September 2012.
Williams was ranked the number one liberal arts college in the country according to U.S. News & World Report at the time.
Williams was a Division III basketball powerhouse, having gone 93–22 over the prior four seasons under head coach Mike Maker.
Duncan Robinson led Williams College to the 2014 NCAA Men's Division III Basketball Tournament championship game.
Duncan Robinson scored 17 points for Williams College in the championship game against University of Wisconsin–Whitewater.
Williams lost in the shadow of a home court scheduling conflict despite 5-6 shooting by Duncan Robinson in the championship game.
Duncan Robinson was the only freshman starter in Mike Maker's six-year tenure as head coach at Williams.
Duncan Robinson was twice named New England Small College Athletic Conference (NESCAC) Player of the Week during his 2013–14 freshman season at Williams.
Williams reached the 2014 NCAA Men's Division III Basketball Tournament championship game, but fell to University of Wisconsin–Whitewater.
Duncan Robinson set school records for single-season minutes played and freshman-season points scored in his 2013–14 season at Williams.
Duncan Robinson led the NECSAC in three-point field goal percentage and minutes played during his 2013–14 season at Williams.
Duncan Robinson was named NESCAC Rookie of the Year and a Second Team All-NESCAC selection after his 2013–14 season at Williams.
Duncan Robinson became Williams' first freshman to be named All-American (4th team, D3Hoops.com) after his 2013–14 season at Williams.
Duncan Robinson was the first D3Hoops.com National Rookie of the Year after his 2013–14 season at Williams.
Duncan Robinson became the first freshman to be named NCAA All-Tournament Team selection after his 2013–14 season at Williams.
Duncan Robinson became the first freshman to score 500 points in a season after his 2013–14 season at Williams.
Maker left Williams to become the head coach for Marist Red Foxes after the 2013–14 season.
Robinson was immediately contacted by schools from various conferences after his freshman success.
Duncan Robinson had decided that he would only leave Williams to play for a winning program that was an elite academic institution and used a system and style similar to what he was accustomed to.
Duncan Robinson asked Maker to contact John Beilein at Michigan, who replied on faith that Michigan may have interest in him as a walk-on player.
Duncan Robinson was not interested in the walk-on consideration given competing scholarship offers.
A week later, after seeing video, Beilein said Michigan was considering a scholarship offer for Duncan Robinson.
Duncan Robinson scheduled visits to Michigan and new Atlantic 10 member Davidson.
After the visit to Michigan, Duncan Robinson committed to the school.
Duncan Robinson announced his decision via Twitter on August 6, 2014.
Duncan Robinson is the only other player to transfer from Division III to Division I with a full scholarship according to some sources.
During the 2014–15 NCAA Division I season, Duncan Robinson redshirted for the Michigan Wolverines.
In December 2014, with assistant coach Jeff Meyer as his rebounder, Duncan Robinson broke Stauskas' Michigan Wolverines practice record for three-pointers in a drill by posting 78.
Duncan Robinson's second game for the 2015–16 Michigan Wolverines was against Elon on November 16, 2015.
On December 1, 2015, Duncan Robinson posted 17 points with 5-7 three-point shooting in a game against NC State.
On December 12, 2015, Duncan Robinson made his first career start for Michigan by posting 11 points on 3-5 three-point shooting.
At the time, Duncan Robinson ranked third in the nation in three-point shooting percentage.
Duncan Robinson tied his career high with six assists against Bryant on December 23, 2014.
The game marked the ninth consecutive game in which he made at least three three-point shots.

Duncan Robinson entered conference play as the Big Ten leader in three-point field goal percentage and led the Big Ten Conference in both three-point field goals (52) and three-point field goal percentage (.565).
On January 12, 2016, with leading scorer Caris LeVert sidelined, Michigan defeated Maryland 70-67 as Duncan Robinson contributed 17 points on 5-9 three-point shooting.
On January 23, 2016, Michigan defeated Nebraska 81-68 behind a game-high and season-high 21 points by Duncan Robinson.
The January 27 game against Rutgers marked the 17th consecutive game in which Duncan Robinson made at least two three-point shots.
Duncan Robinson was held to 0-3 in three-point shooting in the February 6 Michigan–Michigan State rivalry game, ending a 22-game streak of making at least one three-point shot.
On February 10, 2016, Michigan defeated Minnesota as Duncan Robinson recorded his first double-double with 13 points and a season-high 11 rebounds.
Duncan Robinson finished the season second to Bryn Forbes among Big Ten players in three-point field goal percentage with a 45.0% mark.

Several other wing players left the team following the previous season, including Caris LeVert's graduation, Aubrey Dawkins' transfer to UCF, and Kameron Chatman's announcement of his intention to transfer.
Duncan Robinson mostly came off the bench during the 2017–18 season, although he did start one game due to a bookkeeping error on December 17 against Maryland Eastern Shore.
Late in the season, Duncan Robinson began producing The Dak and Dunc Show podcast with teammate Andrew Dakich for WCBN-FM Sports.
The team won the 2017 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament and reached the sweet sixteen round of the 2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament.
Duncan Robinson began his senior season with a team-high 21 points against North Florida on November 11, 2017.
In the game, Duncan Robinson and Charles Matthews became the first Michigan teammates to score 20 points in a game since March 3, 2015.
On January 13, 2018, Isaiah Livers replaced Duncan Robinson in the starting lineup for Michigan when they faced Michigan State in their rivalry game.
With Livers sidelined on February 11, 2018, Duncan Robinson returned to the starting lineup and recorded 16 points, including 14 points in the first half in an 83-72 victory over Wisconsin.
On February 14, 2018, Duncan Robinson recorded 18 points on a season-high six three-point shots in a 74-59 victory over Iowa.
With his six three-pointers in the game, Duncan Robinson surpassed Zack Novak for sixth all-time on Michigan's career three-point leaderboard with 215 for his career.
Duncan Robinson was named the Big Ten Sixth Man of the Year by the coaches following the 2017–18 Big Ten Conference regular season.

On March 1, 2018, in the 2018 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament, Duncan Robinson helped lead Michigan to a 77-71 overtime victory over Iowa after his co-captains, Wagner and Abdur-Rahkman, fouled out by converting a go-ahead three-point shot with 2:17 remaining in overtime.
The following day in the quarterfinals of the Big Ten tournament, Duncan Robinson scored his 1,000th career point on his second three-point field goal of the first half.
Duncan Robinson finished the game with 16 points off the bench, including four three-pointers in a 77-58 victory over Nebraska.
Duncan Robinson averaged 11 points per game during Michigan's four games and helped them win the tournament championship.
On March 21, 2018, Duncan Robinson became an Academic All-Big Ten honoree.
The team lost in the 2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game to Villanova.
Duncan Robinson was the first player to play in both an NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game and a Division III championship game.

Since the team reached the championship games of both the Big Ten tournament and the NCAA Tournament, Duncan shares the Michigan (and NCAA) single-season games played record with teammates Abdur-Rahkman, Jon Teske, Zavier Simpson, and Matthews at 41 games.
Over the course of three seasons, Duncan Robinson finished his career with 237 made three-point shots (on 41.9% shooting), placing fourth on Michigan's all-time list.
After going undrafted in the 2018 NBA draft, Duncan Robinson signed an NBA Summer League contract with the Miami Heat.
In five Summer League games, Duncan Robinson averaged 12.4 points and 2.4 rebounds while shooting 58% (22-for-38) from the field including 63% (17-for-27) on three-point shots.
Duncan Robinson agreed to a two-way contract with the Miami Heat and Sioux Falls Skyforce on July 10, 2018.
When Duncan Robinson made his NBA debut, it was the first by a former Division III player since Devean George.
It was the first ever by a Williams Eph.
Duncan Robinson joined Big X, a team composed of former Big Ten players, in The Basketball Tournament 2018.

Although the Heat's formal training camp did not begin until September 25, 2018, Duncan Robinson declined an invitation to participate as part of the G League-manned squad that Team USA used from September 6 through September 17 to qualify for the 2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup so that he could participate in informal developmental training with the Heat.

When the Heat began the season with four injured players (Wayne Ellington, Justise Winslow, James Johnson, and Dion Waiters), Duncan Robinson and fellow two-way player Yante Maten made the official October 15 opening day roster.
The team began the season with 14 players under full NBA contracts.
When the G League training camps opened on October 22, Duncan Robinson stayed with the Heat.
Duncan Robinson made his NBA debut in the Heat's fourth game of the season on October 24, against the New York Knicks, scoring three points and four rebounds in 10 minutes of action.
He made his first field goal attempt, a three-point shot.
On November 3, 2018, Duncan Robinson scored 23 points as a starter when Sioux Falls opened its season on November 2 with a 112-101 victory against the Fort Wayne Mad Ants.
On December 10, 2018, Duncan Robinson went 10 for 17 on three-point shot attempts against the Agua Caliente Clippers, posting 32 points, 7 rebounds, and 6 assists.
Duncan Robinson scored five points in his first NBA start on February 25, 2019, against the Phoenix Suns.
On March 19, 2019, Duncan Robinson posted his G-League best 36 points against the Oklahoma City Blue.

Duncan Robinson was a 2019 All-NBA G League Third Team selection after posting 21.4 points with a 51.4 percent field goal percentage and 48.3 three-point percentage along with 4.3 rebounds and three assists in 33 games, which resulted in his contract being converted to a standard two-year contract on April 9.
Duncan Robinson established two Skyforce franchise records: Single-season three-point shots made (157), career three-point shot percentage (48.5%, min 200 attempts).
The career three-point shot percentage is an NBA G-League all-time record.
Duncan Robinson led the G League in minutes per game that season (36.9).
Duncan Robinson closed the season with his first double-digit scoring effort with 15 points against the Brooklyn Nets on April 10, 2019.
During the 2019 off-season, Duncan Robinson's contract became a $1 million guarantee with the possibility of a $1.4 million guarantee if he remained on the roster through midseason.
He bulked up 15 pounds (6.8 kg) prior to the 2019-20 season.
With Jimmy Butler sidelined on October 27, 2019, Duncan Robinson posted a then career-high 21 points against the Minnesota Timberwolves.
On November 3, 2019, Duncan Robinson posted 23 points on 7-for-11 three-point shooting against the Houston Rockets.

On November 20, 2019, Duncan Robinson posted a career-high 29 points against his college coach John Beilein's Cleveland Cavaliers, establishing Heat records with seven three-point shots in a quarter and eight in a half.
On December 1, 2019, Duncan Robinson posted a 10-rebound/10-point double-double against the Brooklyn Nets.

On December 10, 2019 (the one-year anniversary of his first professional 10 three-point shot performance), Duncan Robinson scored an NBA career-high 34 points, making 10 three-pointers, that tied a Heat franchise record for three-pointers made in a game, in a 135-121 overtime win against the Atlanta Hawks.
In that game teammate Kendrick Nunn added 36 points, establishing an NBA record for points by an undrafted duo (70).
Following his performance, The Wall Street Journal called Duncan Robinson "the most improbable player in the NBA" and "one of the best shooters on the planet" in an article on December 13, 2019.

On February 12, 2020, against Utah, Duncan Robinson posted his 200th NBA three-point shot in just his 69th career game, the fastest in NBA history, surpassing Donovan Mitchell and Luka Dončić (84 games).
Duncan Robinson appeared as a competitor in the Three-Point Contest at the 2020 NBA All-Star Game.
On March 4, 2020, against Orlando, Duncan Robinson posted nine three-point shots (including seven in a row at one point).
On March 6, 2020, Duncan Robinson scored 24 points and had five rebounds and four assists in a 110-104 loss to the New Orleans Pelicans, shooting 8-of-14 on three-pointers.

His eight three pointers raised his single-season total to 233 with 19 games remaining, passing Wayne Ellington's single-season Heat three-pointers record (227), Damon Jones's NBA undrafted player single-season three-pointers record (225), and Kyle Korver's NBA single-season record for most by a first or second year player (226).

The performance set Robinson up for two more record chases on March 8: tie with Rafer Alston for most consecutive games by a Heat player with at least one three-pointer (49) and George McCloud's NBA record largest increase in made three pointers from one season to the next (223).
On March 8 against the Washington Wizards, Duncan Robinson's former roommate, Mo Wagner got him riled up enough to earn his first technical foul.

In that March 8 contest, Duncan Robinson went 7 for 11 on three point shots and tied Alston with 49 consecutive games with a three-point conversion, a streak that ran for 57 (from game 16 to game 72, the last of the season).

Duncan Robinson was also on pace to smash other NBA records: three-point percentage of field goals attempts (88.3 percent of Robinson's shots were threes vs. the NBA record of 82.7% by Wayne Ellington, minimum 400 attempts) and fewest two-point field goal attempts.
He finished the COVID-shortened 2019-20 NBA season with 270 three point shots made.

For the season, Duncan Robinson set several Heat franchise single-season shooting records: Effective field goal percentage (.667), True shooting percentage (.684) and two-point field goal percentage (.654).
